 PlayStation 5 Security Researcher Claims To Have Dumped Game Binary On GTA 6 Required Firmware, Yet Sony Stays One Step Ahead With New Firmware Update
 Francesco De Meo • 
 Nov 17, 2026 at 06:00am EST 
 Comments 
 Add to Preferred Sources
 A known developer claimed to have dumped a game's binary on Grand Theft Auto VI's required PlayStation 5 firmware, but Sony is again one step ahead 
 In the past few weeks, Sony and PlayStation 5 jailbreakers have been locked in a firmware war , which has forced the Japanese company to release multiple minor firmware updates to prevent users from dumping Grand Theft Auto VI and emulating it or porting it to PC ahead of its inevitable official release. And in the final days before the launch of the game, this war has only intensified.
 "Guess I am the first who dumped game binary at PS5 14.22," wrote known security researcher and developer Gezine on X . While the developer is known to never release their findings nor elaborate on their methods, the developer made more than a few hopeful that Grand Theft Auto VI emulation on PC would take its first steps already on November 19 , as firmware 14.22 is reportedly required to run the game.
 Related Story GTA 6 Hits Early 99 Metascore With 115 Reviews, Beating Zelda: Ocarina of Time as The Best-Reviewed Game of All Time 
 However, these hopes were squashed by Sony itself today. The Japanese company launched a new system software update , 26.07-14.23.00 , whose patch notes leave no doubt as to its purpose: "We’ve made some security fixes to the system software." As such, it's very likely whichever method Gezine used to dump the unspecified game binary on firmware 14.22 has been patched, though it has not yet been confirmed whether Grand Theft Auto VI will require firmware 14.23 at launch.
 While consoles getting jailbroken is nothing new, advances in  AI  are making it increasingly challenging for manufacturers to keep their systems as hack-free as possible . And seeing how the first unofficial PlayStation 5-to-PC ports are starting to come in, it's not surprising to see Sony patch the PlayStation 5 firmware as frequently as possible. 
 While there's little chance that an emulated Grand Theft Auto VI or an unofficial port will make a massive negative impact on the game's sales , it would definitely have one on the relationship between Rockstar Games and Sony , as the Japanese company is the side set to benefit the most, considering the vast majority of pre-orders are for the PlayStation 5 release.
